description: Tool calls, Microsoft Graph calls, HTTP traffic and pod health of the Office 365 MCP server.

panels.title: End of the selected range: state now, counts for the last hour

panels.description: Alerts that fire now for this server: its own alerts and the Kubernetes alerts on its pods and deployment. Open Alerting to see which.

targets.expr: count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", namespace=~"$namespace", alertGroup="office-365-mcp"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing", namespace=~"$namespace", alertGroup=~"kubernetes-application|kubernetes-resources", pod=~"($container)-.+"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing", namespace=~"$namespace", alertGroup="kubernetes-application", deployment=~"$container"}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Firing alerts

panels.description: Pods that pass the readiness probe now. The probe reads the OAuth store in Postgres. Red at 0: every call and every sign-in fails. Office365McpDown fires after 5 minutes at 0.
panels.title: Ready pods

panels.description: Memory that the busiest pod uses now, as a part of its container limit. Orange from 80% (Office365McpMemoryHigh after 30 minutes), red from 90% (KubernetesPodNearMemoryLimit). The pod is OOM-killed at 100%.
panels.title: Memory, % of limit

panels.description: Unexpected exceptions or returned error results (tool_outcomes_total outcome="error") divided by all recorded tool outcomes in the last hour. Graph failures, refused tokens and deliberate refusals are not in the numerator, but they are in the denominator. Orange from 5%, red from 10% (Office365McpToolErrors also needs at least 5 errors).
panels.title: Tool unexpected errors, last hour

panels.description: Graph operations in the last hour with status unavailable, failed, error or paging_unending, as a part of all Graph operations. Red from 20%. Office365McpGraphFailing fires only when there are also 10 or more failures, so red alone does not mean that the alert fires.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in the last hour

panels.title: Graph failures, last hour

panels.description: Graph operations in the last hour with status forbidden (401 or 403), as a part of all Graph operations. Red from 20%. Office365McpGraphForbidden fires only when there are also 10 or more refusals, so red alone does not mean that the alert fires.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in the last hour

panels.title: Graph 401 and 403, last hour

panels.description: Graph throttling answers in the last hour that outlived the SDK's retrying. Red above 5 (Office365McpGraphThrottled). Every registered tool starts at zero, so 0 means that no throttling was recorded.
panels.title: Graph throttled, last hour

panels.description: Tool calls in the last hour whose measured duration was more than 60 seconds (graph_slow_operations_total). The measured duration is the one in graph_operation_duration_seconds: it leaves out waits that a tool marks as not Microsoft's, such as a person confirming. A call that the client timed out at 60 seconds is not here when that wait made it long. Red at 3 (Office365McpGraphSlow). Before this counter existed, the stat reads the duration histogram instead, for each pod and tool that has no counter. That value is an estimate: it subtracts two increase() results, which can extrapolate differently and show a slow call that did not happen. Office365McpGraphSlow reads only the counter.

targets.expr: sum((increase(graph_slow_operations_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container"}[1h]) or ignoring (le) (increase(graph_operation_duration_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container"}[1h]) - ignoring (le) increase(graph_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container", le="60.0"}[1h]))))

panels.title: Graph over 60 s, last hour

panels.description: MCP and OAuth requests in the last 15 minutes that got a 5xx answer, as a part of all requests. Red from 5%. Office365McpHttp5xx also needs 5 such answers.

defaults.noValue: No requests in the last 15 minutes

panels.title: HTTP 5xx, last 15 min

panels.description: Tool calls in the last hour. No calls at night and at weekends is normal.
panels.title: Tool calls, last hour

panels.description: 95% of the Graph operations in the last hour took this time or less. Orange from 30 seconds, red from 60 seconds.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in the last hour

panels.title: Graph p95, last hour

panels.description: Failed liveness probes in the last hour. Kubernetes restarts the pod after 6 failures in a row. Single failures occur when the event loop is busy.
panels.title: Liveness failures, last hour

panels.description: Graph token requests in the last hour, by result. refused: Entra answered with an AADSTS code (Office365McpTokenRefused). failed: no AADSTS code, such as a connection error (Office365McpTokenFailing). Each turns red at 5, the count its alert needs.
panels.title: Token refusals and failures, last hour

panels.description: Which tools this deployment is actually asked for.
panels.title: Tool call rate by tool

panels.description: tool_outcomes_total with every outcome except ok and asked, the same set as the "Tool failures" total. graph: a refusal or failure with a Graph failure in its cause chain (see the Microsoft Graph row). token: Entra issued no token. refused: the tool refused the request on purpose, for example a malformed handle. error: an unexpected exception or a returned error result, which Office365McpToolErrors alerts on. cancelled: the client or the server cancelled the call. Pairs that did not fail in the selected range are hidden.

targets.expr: sum by (operation, outcome) (rate(tool_outcomes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container", outcome!~"ok|asked"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (operation, outcome) (sum by (operation, outcome) (increase(tool_outcomes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container", outcome!~"ok|asked"}[$__range] @ end())) > 0)

panels.title: Tool failures by tool and outcome

panels.description: Buckets are set upstream in unique_mcp/monitoring.py and stop at 10 s. A quantile at 10 s means that the rank fell at or past the last finite bucket; this panel cannot tell how far past. This histogram also includes waits for a person to confirm. For tool calls that attempted Graph, read 'Graph operation duration', whose buckets reach 300 s.
panels.title: Tool call duration

panels.description: Graph tokens that tool calls asked for in each interval, counted with increase() like the "Token refusals and failures, last hour" stat. ok includes tokens the SDK serves from its cache. refused is an Entra answer with an AADSTS code; failed is any other failure, such as a network error. A tool call without a token never reaches Graph.
panels.title: Token acquisitions by tool and result

panels.description: Graph operations in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes, by status. Red is a failure. forbidden is a 401 or 403. not_found, cancelled and too_large are answers to the caller.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in this range

panels.title: Graph operations by status

panels.description: One observation per tool call, split by the operation it was counted under. operation is a name chosen in code, one per tool — never a Graph URL. graph_client/observability.py says why that is a hard rule.
panels.title: Graph operation rate

panels.description: status is the remedy class from graph_client/errors.py, not the HTTP code: forbidden (consent or permission), throttled, unavailable (Graph or egress), not_found, paging_unending (a collection Graph would not end), too_large (an answer this connector declined to hold), failed, and error for something that is not a Graph failure at all. not_found and too_large are excluded: a caller asking for a chat or a message that is gone got an answer, not an incident, and an answer over this connector's size ceiling is this connector declining correctly rather than failing. forbidden is included — it almost always means the app registration is missing a delegated permission or an admin consent, which is a deployment defect.
panels.title: Graph failures by operation and status

panels.description: Time of one tool call that attempted Graph, measured by GraphOperationMiddleware: SDK retries, Retry-After waits and every page of a paged walk included. A wait that a tool marks as not Microsoft's, such as a confirmation from a person, is left out. Buckets reach 300 s (views in office_365_mcp/metrics.py).
panels.title: Graph operation duration

panels.description: Which tool is the slow one. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_365_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by operation

panels.description: graph_slow_operations_total for each tool, in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes. It is the counter that Office365McpGraphSlow sums over one hour. It uses the measured duration, which leaves out waits for a person to confirm, and it counts a call whatever its status, cancelled included. Kong and the chat close the request at 60 seconds. Before this counter existed, the panel reads the duration histogram instead, for each pod and tool that has no counter. That value is an estimate: it subtracts two increase() results, which can extrapolate differently and show a slow call that did not happen. Office365McpGraphSlow reads only the counter.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in this range

targets.expr: sum by (operation) ((increase(graph_slow_operations_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container"}[$__rate_interval]) or ignoring (le) (increase(graph_operation_duration_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container"}[$__rate_interval]) - ignoring (le) increase(graph_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", container=~"$container", le="60.0"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Graph operations over 60 seconds by tool

panels.description: retried=true means the SDK spent its retries and Graph was still throttling. retried=false means Graph asked for a wait past the SDK's ceiling and none was attempted — a quota problem rather than a burst.
panels.title: Throttling rate by operation

panels.description: Pages one paged walk read to answer one call. p99 climbing while the call rate is flat is a filter Graph cannot push down: the walk reads pages to throw them away, and the item scan cap is all that stops it.
panels.title: Pages scanned per walk

panels.description: One observation per Graph call inside a tool, which is the call rate the operation panels do not show. A paged walk is one call here however many pages it read — Pages scanned per walk counts those.
panels.title: Graph call rate by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is slow. `operation` is the tool, `step` is the call it made — the panel above says a tool got slower, this one says which of its Graph calls did.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is failing, and how. A step counted `forbidden` while its operation is counted `ok` is a tool recovering — teams_read_transcript falling back to an unattributed transcript is the one that does this by design.
panels.title: Graph failures by step and status

panels.description: Buckets are spelled out one page at a time at the low end (office_365_mcp/metrics.py), because nearly every walk reads exactly one. Mass moving off the bottom row is the signal; a walk that gives up on an unending collection lands just past 10.
panels.title: Pages scanned distribution

panels.description: Inbound HTTP, from unique_toolkit's middleware. /, /health, /ready and /metrics are not counted (setup_ops excludes them), so this is MCP and OAuth traffic only — 401s here are the OAuth handshake, not an outage.
panels.title: HTTP request rate by path and status

panels.description: One inbound MCP request end to end, so it contains the tool call and every Graph call that tool made. This is the only one of the three latency histograms whose buckets this service can choose — via setup_ops(duration_buckets=...) in office_365_mcp/app.py — so it is the panel to read for the slow tail. The layout it wants comes from the Graph timeout budget: 30s per request (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds) times four attempts (max_retries=3) is 120s, plus Retry-After waits, and a paged walk is several requests — hence buckets at 30, 60, 120 and 300 above prometheus_client's defaults, whose own top finite bucket is 10s. Quantiles sitting on the top bucket mean 'past the last bucket'; read the throttling panel next. Only POST is counted: a GET on /mcp is an event stream that stays open for minutes.
panels.title: HTTP request duration

panels.description: One replica serving 30-second Graph calls: this is the queue depth to watch before adding tools, not CPU.
panels.title: Requests in flight

panels.description: Pods that pass the readiness probe. The probe reads the OAuth store in Postgres, so a Postgres outage shows here as 0 while the pod still runs.
panels.title: Ready pods

panels.description: Container restarts per pod in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes.
panels.title: Pod restarts

panels.description: Working set per pod, against the container memory limit. The pod is OOM-killed at the limit. A line that climbs for days and drops at a rollout is memory that the process keeps.
panels.title: Memory usage vs limit

panels.description: CPU cores used per pod, against the CPU request. The container has no CPU limit, so it can use more than the request and is never throttled.
panels.title: CPU usage vs request

panels.description: Failed liveness, readiness and startup probes in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes. Readiness failures at a rollout are normal. Kubernetes restarts the pod after 6 liveness failures in a row.

defaults.noValue: No probe failures in this range

panels.title: Probe failures by probe

panels.description: Out-of-memory kills per pod in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes. Each kill stops all calls that the pod has open.

defaults.noValue: No OOM kills in this range

panels.title: OOM kills
